mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit quarterly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a sharp contraction in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate sales and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative following a >10% quarterly decline in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such INDPRO contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) over a two-month period signals a rapid deterioration in the labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (below 2% for at least six months) combined with low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) signals a prolonged accommodative monetary environment, which supports equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL < 2% for at least 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of both low FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during sustained INDPRO expansions above the 12-month moving average for six months.
